metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Kersey, CO | Weld County DJ Basin
metaDescription: Own minerals under South Platte bottomland near Kersey, CO? We evaluate Wattenberg Niobrara/Codell production and quote against your recent royalty checks.
heroLead: Kersey sits inside dense Wattenberg field development, where South Platte River bottomland and old homestead quarters have been drilled and re-drilled for three decades.
intro: Kersey is unincorporated Weld County along the South Platte, close enough to Greeley that most surrounding sections have seen at least one round of horizontal Niobrara and Codell development since 2010. If your family patented land here in the early 1900s and kept the minerals when it sold, or you inherited a fractional interest from a grandparent's quarter section, you're sitting on some of the most heavily developed acreage in the DJ Basin.

sections.heading: What's producing under Kersey ground
paragraphs: Wattenberg field wells around Kersey typically target the Niobrara B and C benches with a Codell tail, drilled in multi-well pads on 640- or 1280-acre spacing units. Operators have consolidated leases over the years, so a single pad may now be draining several old vertical-well tracts at once. If your mineral deed predates 2010, there's a fair chance your interest has been pooled into a unit you've never seen the boundary map for.

Decline curves on Niobrara horizontals run steep in year one, then flatten into a long stripper-well tail. A 2015-vintage well paying strong checks in 2016 may be down to a fraction of that now, which is exactly the production history a buyer needs before quoting a number.

sections.heading: Split estate and the surface owner problem
paragraphs: Plenty of Kersey mineral owners never lived on the land themselves; the surface sold decades ago while the minerals stayed with the family. That's a clean split estate, but it also means you may not know a well was permitted, spaced, or completed until a division order shows up. Weld County's clerk and recorder keeps the lease and pooling filings, and that's the first place we check when we evaluate an interest here.

Because most of Weld's oil and gas activity sits inside county-level rules rather than dense municipal overlays, Kersey hasn't seen the setback fights nearby cities have faced under SB 19-181 local control. That relative predictability is part of why DJ Basin core acreage still trades steadily even while buyers pull back elsewhere.

sections.heading: What we need to quote your interest
paragraphs: Send your deed or the legal description in section-township-range form, and if you have them, your last two or three division order statements. We match operator, well name, and API number against Colorado Oil and Gas Conservation Commission production records, then quote a range tied to what the unit has actually paid out and how fast it's declining, not a flat number pulled from a chart.

faqs.question: How do I know which operator holds my Kersey lease?
faqs.answer: Your division order statement names the operator and well, or you can search the legal description against Weld County clerk and recorder filings. Send us the section-township-range and we'll run that lookup.

faqs.question: My well was drilled in 2013 — is it still worth selling?
faqs.answer: Yes, though the number reflects where the well sits on its decline curve now, not its early peak. A mature Wattenberg well on a stripper tail has a different value than a fresh completion, and we price it that way.

faqs.question: Do I need a lawyer to sell a fractional interest?
faqs.answer: Not required for a straightforward sale, but if your interest passed through an estate without a clean probate, an attorney can help clear title before closing so the deal doesn't stall.

faqs.question: Will you buy a small fractional interest, like a 1/32nd?
faqs.answer: Yes. Small fractional interests are common in this part of Weld County from land divided across generations, and we quote them scaled to your share.
